findings.detail: The Recommendations set out actions and amounts but do not explain why those actions suit the clients’ objectives, as the specification requires. The historic account figure also adds unnecessary detail to a section meant to stay high level.
report_quote: We recommend disinvesting the joint GIA. We recommend using the gross proceeds of c. £38,000 to fund both Robert’s and Jean’s ISAs for the new tax year.
Your joint General Investment Account was previously shown in our records (10 March) as £30,000.

findings.detail: The meeting note says Jean would find the cash-account paperwork and its balance would be confirmed before anything was finalised; the report mentions the uncertainty but omits that agreed step. It also describes the GIA’s approximate value seen at the meeting as prospective gross sale proceeds, which are not yet known.
report_quote: Jean also mentioned a separate cash account from some years ago, although she is unsure whether it remains active or what it contains.
We recommend using the gross proceeds of c. £38,000 to fund both Robert’s and Jean’s ISAs for the new tax year.

findings.detail: The report silently ignores the handling instruction to refer sensitively to the money’s origin: Jean’s inheritance following her mother’s death. It does not leak the internal guidance wording.
report_quote: The £120,000 will be used together with these proceeds to fund both ISAs for the new tax year.

findings.detail: The repeated ‘We recommend’ makes the advice slightly clumsy to read, though its meaning remains clear.
report_quote:
We recommend the following:

We recommend disinvesting the joint GIA. We recommend using the gross proceeds of c. £38,000

findings.detail: All five markers identify the particular missing amounts, tax point or charge rates and the relevant accounts or platform clearly enough for adviser follow-up.
